title: Conditional κ = 7.54549816771013·10⁻⁴: kernel, target-prefix, plateau and reorder stages on #310's w3 word, priced against #304's complex supplier (+0.138% over #311)
body:
# Conditional κ = 7.54549816771013·10⁻⁴: kernel, target-prefix, plateau and reorder stages on #310's w3 word, priced against #304's complex supplier (+0.138% over #311)

One self-contained package, `research/w3-bitword-stages/` (#310's package with four added transcript stages and a supplier admission), with its own workflow. No existing file is changed.

**κ = 377274908385506513145517/(5·10²⁶) = 7.54549816771013·10⁻⁴**: +0.2200% over #310 (7.52893499605335·10⁻⁴) and +0.1382% over #311 (7.53508664880763·10⁻⁴). Bit coarse 7.5512·10⁻⁴, complex 7.635·10⁻⁴ (#304's supplier): the bit side binds.

## What it adds

#310's w3 word (the PR #249/source527 cohort word with a design-T cube layer, twin condensation and a SAT line-pair module) is admitted by #310 with no transcript stages. This package re-derives the stages of the gen4/gen5 lineage on it and prices against the stronger complex supplier, which becomes necessary: with #233's supplier (7547/10⁷) the complex side would bind at 7.541308566883·10⁻⁴.

| step | items | local Σφ | κ after the step |
|---|---|---:|---|
| #310 | – | 1,068,458.57 | 7.52893499605·10⁻⁴ |
| 1. kernel stage | 433 response-kernel families (twin pairs, integer and F₂ triples, multi-donor families with shared donors on nested chains; multi-seed packing) + 85 zero-response singles; entrance rank 840; 132 new frames | stock 162,123 → 161,843 | 7.53675926616·10⁻⁴ |
| 2. target-prefix + plateau | 45 F₂ target-prefix groups (window dependency R_t = Σ ±R_p, k ≤ 3); 660 identical five-gate components retimed into new dim-15 frames | −1,025.22 | – |
| 3. reorder | just-in-time MOVE normalisation + 172 commuting addition relocations (two rounds, fixed point) | −326.55 | bit cap 7.54549816771·10⁻⁴ |
| 4. complex supplier | #304's program through #309's source-bound adapter, priced at 7635/10⁷ | – | **7.54549816771·10⁻⁴** |

The φ ledger (φ(r) = r·ln(120/r), deficit fixed; ≈ −6.45·10⁻¹⁰ κ per φ on #310's ledger) predicted the stage-2+3 gain at +8.72·10⁻⁷ against +8.74·10⁻⁷ verified. **Reviewer note:** the 85 zero-response singles are helpers that the w3 redesign left without prefix reads; they enter directly at their first frame and are carried as kernel entries without partners (≈ 407 φ). Sinks (582 shape matches), early restorations (440 candidates; they would need final-frame changes that #310's legality checker rejects) and cleanup sandwiches (none on w3) are not composed. #311's 209 squares are bound to record indices on #310's word and were not re-screened on this one; this package's 45 target-prefix groups are its own screen on the kernel word.

## Checks

* Kernel: exact rank and 9I − J Gram nondegeneracy of all 132 new frames; the F₂ kernel identity of every family on the original prefix responses; E inside every member's first frame; no source owner or donor key among members, pivots and donors disjoint; GF(2) replays with random dirty inputs (sources unchanged, targets t ⊕ x, helpers restored, every register equal to #310's); controls omitting the Q and Q⁻¹ gates rejected.
* Target-prefix and plateau: nested chains; forward and inverse F₂ all-column replays; an integer replay mod 2⁶¹ − 1 equal on every register; the exact source-span rule (0 violations).
* Reorder: the screen re-run must reproduce the frozen selection; crossed-interval contract; integer replay; non-vacuous omission control; fixed point.
* #304 supplier: #309's adapter archive pinned by hash and member inventory, extracted fresh, `gx.check1` on the actual #304 program with its label, scalar, splice, cover, router, precision and row guards.
* #310's native chain on the final word: legality (518 selections); all 23,627 global and 22,172 compact F₂ columns (payload 97 bits < 104); exact charts for 4,265 new frames and 22,118 changed projectors (≤ 342 factors); bank review (made generic: census and width-120 tiling read from `stages/bank-tiling.json`, an integer-programming tiling; 105,523 banks per stage, stock 809,215 / 161,843, 3,026,400 assignments); price (two moment engines, eight levels, 47 strict constraints, adjacent grid rejected); finite invoice (coefficient 58,364,056,416,171,201 < 2⁸⁰, selector 571,950,117,600 < 2⁴⁰).

## Verify

    sudo apt-get install -y g++ libboost-dev
    python3 -m pip install -r research/w3-bitword-stages/requirements.txt
    python3 -B research/w3-bitword-stages/verify.py --output /tmp/w3-stages-proof --cxx g++    # about 20 minutes

Passes on macOS (clang++) and on Linux (g++). The workflow (#310's, renamed, 60-minute limit) runs it on Ubuntu. `supplied/base/249-DONOR-OWNERSHIP.json` keeps #310's exact bytes through a package `.gitattributes` (`-text`), so the manifest matches a fresh checkout.

## Scope

Conditional finite construction under #310's inherited all-size interfaces (compiler, common weighted charts, restored rows, selectors, routing, prime supply, complex dirty lifting, precision/recovery, analytic transfer). No Lean proof, unconditional theorem or runtime result is claimed. #310, #309 and #304 are open; their word, admission and supplier are inherited unchanged except the generic bank-tiling input and re-pinned literals.

## Credits

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0; lineage in `NOTICE.md` (#310's notice kept as `NOTICE-PR310.md`). The w3 word and its admission are utcorvusvolat-dotcom's (#310, from a supplied archive of two agents' builders); the stronger complex supplier is DreamingOfClouds' (#304) through Dugongue's source-bound adapter (#309); the kernel mechanism is Dugongue's (#254/#259/#272) in our multi-donor form (#266/#282/#290); the target-prefix mechanism is eumemic's (#268) with rohanarun's native stages (#273/#311); the reorder stage is ours (#299/#306). This package contributes the four stages on the w3 word, the generic bank tiling and the composition.



**Repository CI.** This branch includes PR #318's unchanged three-file joint-dual source-pin repair (certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json, certificates/joint-dual-validation.json, research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json), as #366 and #368 do, so the repository-wide `verify (joint)` job passes. No mathematics is changed by it.
